title: Identifying target markets
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank teaches choosing a target market through mass marketing, segmentation or a niche; market research for a new business is a related idea, not the same one.

draft.title: Identifying target markets
card: A target market is the group of customers a business chooses to aim its marketing at. The business can choose it in three main ways.
selling one product with one marketing mix to the whole market, such as basic salt sold to almost every household.
splitting the market into groups with shared traits, such as age, income or location, then aiming at one or more of those groups with a marketing mix for each.
aiming at one small, specialised part of the market, such as hiking boots made only for people with wide feet.
draft.remember: A business picks its target market: everyone, chosen segments, or one small niche.

a.q: A bakery in Orange makes gluten-free cakes only for people with coeliac disease. Which approach is this?
a.why: The bakery aims at one small, specialised part of the market, which is niche marketing. It is not mass marketing, because it does not aim at nearly everyone.
a.clue: Is the bakery aiming at everyone or at one small group?

b.q: Priya runs a gym chain in Perth. She offers early-morning classes for workers, daytime classes for retirees and a junior program for teenagers, each with its own price and promotion. Which approach is this?
b.why: Priya splits the market into groups by shared traits and uses a different marketing mix for each, which is market segmentation. Niche marketing is the tempting answer, but it aims at only one small, specialised part of the market, not several groups.
b.clue: Count how many groups she aims at and how many marketing mixes she uses.
